more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
Approved in the US.
US food use is subject to the listed CFR provisions and their conditions, checked in 2026.
more_info.overview: Carrageenan is used as an emulsifier in food. Its technological role is to help oil and water remain mixed.
more_info.uses: EU permissions include milk-based drinks and similar products intended for young children, unflavoured pasteurised cream (excluding reduced fat creams), unflavoured live fermented cream products and substitute products, both with a fat  content of less than 20 %, jam jellies and marmalades and similar products. These permissions depend on the food category and its conditions of use.
more_info.daily_intake: 75 mg/kg body weight/day, combined carrageenan and processed Eucheuma seaweed; temporary in the 2018 EFSA assessment.
more_info.origin: Extracted from red seaweeds with water or dilute alkali. Food-grade carrageenan contains large sulphated polysaccharides and is distinct from deliberately degraded carrageenan.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: The specified starting material is plant derived and compatible with vegetarian and vegan diets. The specification does not establish halal or kosher certification.
more_info.side_effects:
The review found no genotoxicity or cancer concern in the available food-grade studies.
Composition, exposure and toxicology uncertainties led to a temporary intake limit.
